data.name: Excubitor
data.detailed_description:
Steam Greenlight


Acerca do jogo


Upgrade your ship, fortify your defences and ready your weapons, because you’re going to need all the help you can get!

Armed to the teeth and set on sheer destruction, waves of enemy drones are rushing towards the mothership, Antares. You must strategically build your defences in the best possible locations as you take direct control of your Hammerhead defence craft equipped with the deadliest weapons such as; the multi-targeting Tesla Coil, the helium plasma Combustor or the devastating Decimator.


  • Equip the Hammerhead with 17 upgradable weapons that Michael Bay would be proud of!
  • Upgrade the various subsystems of The Hammerhead. Increase your rate of fire with the berserk ability or stun enemies with the shockwave ability, plus more.
  • Defeat colossal sized bosses in epic battles!
  • Strategically build and upgrade 9 turrets Use the Prism turret that bounces lasers off multiple enemies or the high damage, high accuracy, Gatling laser.
  • Interact with the environment to aid your defence.
  • Four levels of difficulty to challenge even the most experienced players, including NewGame+, the hardest game mode we've ever created! ...featuring new super secret weapons.
  • Replay any level in order to achieve the highest score and gold rank.


In 1935, Albert Einstein and Nathan Rosen predicted the existence of wormholes; shortcuts through space-time enabling instantaneous travel across vast regions of space. A century later, a discovery was made that turned their theory into reality - plunging mankind into an interstellar space race to claim the ultimate prize: the Voidshards.

The events of Excubitor are set in the year 2182, in a remote star system colonized by humans. At its heart is the Baphomet - a vast ‘hyper-giant’, a star over a thousand times larger than our own sun and one of the biggest stars known to humanity. Dozens, maybe even hundreds of planets orbit the giant star, with many more swallowed up as Baphomet grew larger during its stellar evolution. All around the system, a strange and powerful element is scattered across the many worlds. An element that could provide humanity with all the energy it will ever need. An element that takes the form of blue crystals known as the Voidshards.

data.short_description: In this classic inspired Tower Defense Bullet Hell Shooter, security bots have revolted and you, the sole surviving pilot, are all that stands between the colonies and defeat. Upgrade your ship, weapons and turrets whilst facing a plethora of enemies and colossal bosses. Why did the drones turn?

reviews.review:
Excubitor is a hybrid action and strategy game developed by Tesseract Interactive and published by Kasedo Games. Set in a futuristic era where humanity has spread across the galaxy, the game places players in command of the Hammerhead defense craft during a desperate struggle against autonomous machines that have unexpectedly turned hostile. While the story serves primarily as a framework for the gameplay, it establishes an intriguing science-fiction setting filled with advanced technology, distant colonies, and the valuable Voidshards that power human expansion. The campaign gradually reveals the conflict while giving players a clear motivation to defend the Antares mothership and the remaining human settlements from overwhelming robotic forces.

What immediately distinguishes Excubitor from other indie action titles is its seamless combination of twin-stick shooting and tower defense mechanics. Instead of choosing between direct combat or strategic planning, players must excel at both simultaneously. Every mission requires constant movement to dodge incoming projectiles while constructing, positioning, and upgrading defensive turrets that help contain the growing enemy assault. This balance keeps every encounter engaging because success depends not only on fast reactions but also on careful preparation and efficient resource management. The game rarely allows players to become complacent, as every wave introduces new threats that force them to adjust their tactics on the fly.

The combat system offers a satisfying amount of customization through an extensive collection of upgradeable weapons and ship enhancements. Players gradually unlock an arsenal that supports different combat styles, whether focusing on sustained fire, electrical attacks, explosive damage, or powerful area-of-effect abilities. Complementing these weapons are special ship abilities that can temporarily shift the momentum of battle during particularly intense encounters. Since upgrades persist throughout the campaign, there is a rewarding sense of progression that encourages experimentation with different loadouts and strategies rather than relying on a single approach.

The tower defense component adds meaningful depth rather than functioning as a secondary mechanic. Multiple turret types each fulfill distinct battlefield roles, allowing players to create defensive networks suited to specific mission layouts. Some towers excel at eliminating weaker enemies, while others specialize in targeting heavily armored opponents or controlling large groups through unique attack patterns. Proper placement becomes increasingly important as later missions introduce more aggressive enemy formations, making strategic planning just as valuable as precise shooting. The interaction between active combat and automated defenses creates an experience that feels dynamic throughout every level.

Enemy design contributes significantly to the game's challenge. Standard drones gradually give way to more specialized robotic opponents with varying attack behaviors and movement patterns, ensuring that players must continually adapt instead of repeating the same strategy. Massive boss encounters serve as memorable highlights, combining complex attack patterns with relentless pressure that tests both combat skill and defensive planning. These battles effectively showcase the game's hybrid design by demanding mastery of every mechanic introduced during the campaign.

Visually, Excubitor embraces a vibrant futuristic aesthetic filled with glowing energy weapons, colorful explosions, and detailed science-fiction environments. The visual effects successfully capture the excitement of classic arcade shooters while maintaining enough clarity for players to navigate the screen despite the intense volume of bullets and enemies. The soundtrack complements the action with energetic electronic music that reinforces the fast-paced atmosphere, while impactful sound effects make every weapon discharge and enemy explosion feel satisfying.

Replayability is another strength. The campaign encourages players to revisit completed stages to achieve higher rankings, improve their performance, and unlock additional upgrades. Multiple difficulty levels make the game accessible to newcomers while still providing a demanding experience for veterans seeking a true challenge. New Game Plus further extends longevity by introducing stronger enemies and additional surprises, giving experienced players a reason to continue refining their strategies after completing the main story.

The game is not entirely without flaws. Managing both ship combat and defensive construction can feel overwhelming during the early hours, especially for players unfamiliar with either genre. The learning curve is noticeably steep, and certain missions require multiple attempts before effective strategies become apparent. While the campaign remains enjoyable throughout, it is relatively brief, meaning much of the long-term appeal comes from replaying missions, improving rankings, and tackling higher difficulty settings rather than discovering entirely new content.

Overall, Excubitor succeeds because it confidently blends two genres that rarely work together this effectively. Its engaging mix of arcade shooting, strategic tower placement, rewarding progression system, and challenging boss encounters creates a distinctive experience that stands apart from more conventional shooters or tower defense games. Although its demanding gameplay may not appeal to everyone, players who enjoy mastering complex mechanics and overcoming increasingly difficult battles will find plenty to appreciate. It delivers a polished and rewarding science-fiction adventure that rewards both quick reflexes and thoughtful planning, making it a worthwhile choice for fans of action and strategy alike.

Rating: 6/10
